ENGLISH — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. going
   C. goed
   D. went

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

5. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a joining word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a describing word

7. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

8. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

9. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

10. When practising Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

11. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

12. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

13. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

14. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

15. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for the main idea and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 3.2.1. Reading: Information and Meaning and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 3.5.1 Writing Narrative Paragraphs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar 4.3.1 Verbs and Tense and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
